A 75-year-old female patient seeks medical attention with a 3-month history of progressive leg edema,
exertional dyspnea, and abdominal discomfort. She reports nausea and poor appetite, leading to a
6-kg weight loss. Her medical history includes ovarian cancer treated with paclitaxel and two
pulmonary embolic events in the past year. She has a 25-pack-year smoking history and consumes
two glasses of wine daily. Physical examination reveals a fatigued-appearing woman with the following
measurements and vital signs: height 164 cm, weight 54 kg, BMI 20 kg/m2, temperature 37.0°C, pulse
110/min, respirations 13/min, and blood pressure 143/86 mm Hg. Notable findings include icteric
conjunctivae, abdominal distention with positive fluid wave and shifting dullness, 2+ lower extremity
pitting edema, clear lung sounds, and jugular venous distention. What is the most probable cause of
these clinical findings? Answer Choices: (A) Obstruction of the hepatic veins (B) Superior vena cava
syndrome (C) Peritoneal carcinomatosis (D) Right ventricular failure (E) Liver cirrhosis (F) Portal vein
thrombosis (G) Liver metastases (H) Hypoalbuminemia (I) Constrictive pericarditis (J) Nephrotic
syndrome
 A. Hypoalbuminemia
B. Liver metastases
C. Obstruction of the hepatic veins
D. Superior vena cava syndrome
E. Peritoneal carcinomatosis
F. Nephrotic syndrome
G. Right ventricular failure
H. Liver cirrhosis
I. Portal vein thrombosis

J. Constrictive pericarditis
